full_judgment:
FRM Nazmul Ahasan J: On an application under article 102(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Judgment and Order dated 19.8.2001 rejecting Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 2001 under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure and order dated 6-6-2001, 19-8-2001and 15-10-2001 in Title Execution Case No. 23 of 1995 passed by the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat 4th Court, Dhaka confirming auction and executing and registering Sale Certificate shall not be declared as illegal, null, void, without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and also as to why the said auction dated 6-6-2001 and all subsequent action taken thereof in Title Execution Case No. 23 of 1995 shall not be declared as without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. 

 2. The petitioner, Rupali Bank Ltd. (shortly, the Bank) as decree-holder filed Title Execution Case No. 23 of 1995 against respondent Nos. 2-4 for recovery of Taka 7,85,767 including interest as on 31-5-1995 by sale of mortgaged property of 1.20 acres of land situated in Police Station Savar, District-Dhaka. The said Title Execution Case arose out of final decree dated 7-9-1994 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka in Title Suit No.74 of 1993. Thereafter on 6-6-2001 date was fixed for auction and as per auction notice published in the daily newspaper the auction was fixed to be held at 12 noon. But that auction practically held at 4 pm; that the respondent No. 5 and two others participated in the auction and respondent No.5 made highest bid for an amount of Taka 1,50,000 for 1.20 acres of land in a fine area within Police Station Savar, that the bid money was hopelessly little and the petitioner Bank instantly raised objection and filed application on the same date on 6-6-2001 for cancellation of the auction. But the learned Judge of the Adalat without giving any findings rejected the application; that thereafter, the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 2001 under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating that the present market value of 1.20 acres of land in that locality is at least Taka 30,00,000 and the value of the auction is excessively low but the learned Judge of the Adalat by order dated 19-8-2001 rejected the Miscellaneous Case and also confirmed the auction sale; that subsequently, the petitioner Bank filed an application on 12-9-2001 praying for staying all further proceedings of the Execution Case No. 23 of 1995 stating that the petitioner Bank will move the matter to the Higher Court against the order dated 19-8-2001 but the learned Judge of the Adalat fixed next date on 14-10-2001 for hearing, but without disposal of the petition, the learned Judge of the Adalat passed art order on 17-9-2001 for preparation of sale certificate and executed sale certificate on 15-10-2001 and the same was registered on 15-10-2001. 

 7. It appears from the annexure-A to the Writ Petition that the petitioner filed a written objection in the Execution case No. 23 of 1995 stating that the bid money is hopelessly low value and the Bank will suffer huge loss. It further appears from annexure-Al, order No. 58 dated 6-6-2001 which reads as follows: 

 15. The impugned judgment and order dated 19-8-2001 passed by the learned joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 2001 is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. Consequently, all further auction taken by the learned Judge of the Adalat by order dated 6-6-2001, 19-8-2001 and 15-10-2001 in Title Execution Case No. 23 of 1995 are also declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 16. The learned Judge of the Adalat is directed to proceed further with the execution case in accordance with law.
